In a cohort of 412 participants followed for a median of 4.6 years, plasma neurofilament light chain concentrations rose measurably in the 18 months before symptom onset in those who later developed the disease. Levels were quantified using single-molecule array assays, with intra-assay coefficients of variation below 8 percent. A model combining baseline concentration, age, and rate of change achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.87 for predicting conversion within two years (95% confidence interval 0.81 to 0.92). Sensitivity was 0.79 at a specificity of 0.85. The authors caution that the cohort was drawn from specialized clinics and that performance may be lower in the general population, where comorbid conditions also raise the marker. Replication in an independent cohort is under way.
